INTRODUCTION
Welcome to Your Comprehensive Scheme of Work Resource
About This Ebook
Welcome to this comprehensive collection of Schemes of Work for Pre-primary and Primary 
education, covering the complete educational journey from Prenursery through Primary 6 
(ages 2-12 years). This resource provides detailed, term-by-term curriculum guidance for all 
essential subjects across all class levels.
Official Curriculum Alignment
This Scheme of Work is fully aligned with Nigerian educational authorities:
FOR PRIMARY EDUCATION (Primary 1-6): Completely aligned with the Nigerian 
Educational Research and Development Council (NERDC) - the Federal Government's 
curriculum authority - ensuring full compliance with national standards, learning objectives, 
and assessment frameworks.
FOR EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATION (Prenursery - Nursery 3): Fully aligned with 
the National Association of Proprietors of Private Schools (NAPPS) curriculum 
framework, meeting recognized standards for quality pre-primary education.
This dual alignment ensures regulatory compliance, quality assurance, and confidence for 
administrators, teachers, parents, and educational authorities.
Coverage
PRE-PRIMARY (NAPPS-Aligned): Prenursery, Nursery 1, 2, 3
PRIMARY (NERDC-Aligned): Primary 1-6
ALL ESSENTIAL SUBJECTS
The 13-Week Structure
Each term follows this proven format:
•
Weeks 1-4: New content introduction
•
Week 5: Mid-term Assessment
•
Week 6: Mid-term Break
•
Weeks 7-10: Advanced content
•
Week 11: Comprehensive Revision

•
Week 12: End of Term Examination
•
Week 13: Closing & Awards
Key Features
✓Officially Compliant - Meets NERDC and NAPPS standards
✓Age-Appropriate - Content matched to developmental stages
✓Comprehensive - Complete curriculum coverage
✓Detailed - Week-by-week guidance with full content breakdown
✓Progressive - Logical skill building from simple to complex
✓Practical - Ready for immediate classroom implementation
✓Holistic - Academic, social, emotional, physical, and moral development
✓Flexible - Adaptable while maintaining curriculum requirements
Getting Started
1. Select your class level
2. Review the complete term structure
3. Prepare necessary resources
4. Implement with confidence knowing you are meeting all official requirements
5. Track progress against national standards
6. Celebrate achievements
Our Commitment
These schemes represent a commitment to both educational excellence and full regulatory 
compliance. Every topic has been carefully planned to ensure children receive quality 
education while schools meet all NERDC (Primary) and NAPPS (Early Childhood) 
requirements.
From Prenursery to Primary 6, this ebook provides structured guidance that transforms 
classrooms while satisfying regulatory standards.
Welcome to structured excellence in education—where quality meets compliance!

Fully aligned with NERDC (Nigerian Educational Research and Development Council) for Primary 
and NAPPS (National Association of Proprietors of Private Schools) for Early Childhood Education.
Ready to begin? Turn the page and let's start with Prenursery!

cells.Teacher's Activities: i. Teacher uses songs and rhymes to introduce body parts. ii.Teacher points to and names body parts (head, hands, legs, face, body). iii.Teacher uses charts and pictures to show the body. iv. Teacher guides pupils to touch and identify their own body parts. v. Teacher shows pictures of clean, healthy children.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i.Pupils sing body parts songs. ii. Pupils point to their body parts. iii.Pupils touch their body parts when named. iv.Pupils look at pictures of children. v. Pupils say "body" with teacher.
cells.Learning Resources: Charts Pictures Dolls Mirrors Body parts poster Video clips

weeks.topic: Care of the Skin I - Bathing Regularly

cells.Teacher's Activities: i.Teacher uses charts and video clips to explain bathing in simple terms. ii. Teacher demonstrates bathing using a doll with water, soap, and sponge. iii. Teacher sings bathing songs ("This is the way we wash our body"). iv. Teacher emphasizes bathing every day. v. Teacher shows pictures of children taking baths.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i.Pupils watch bathing demonstration. ii.Pupils sing bathing songs. iii.Pupils mime washing their body. iv.Pupils identify water, soap, and sponge. v. Pupils practice with dolls.
cells.Learning Resources: Doll Basin Water Soap Sponge Towel Charts Pictures Video clips

weeks.topic:
Care of the Skin II
- Applying Body Cream

cells.Teacher's Activities:
i. Teacher demonstrates drying
body with towel after bathing using a doll. ii.Teacher shows how to apply body cream and hair cream. iii.Teacher lets pupils touch and smell body cream. iv.Teacher emphasizes applying cream after bathing. v. Teacher shows pictures of children applying cream.
cells.Pupil's Activities:
i. Pupils mime drying their body.
ii.Pupils pretend to apply body cream. iii.Pupils touch body cream containers. iv.Pupils identify towel and cream. v. Pupils practice on dolls.
cells.Learning Resources:
Towel Body cream
Hair cream Lotion Charts Pictures Dolls Video clips

weeks.topic: Care of the Skin III - Materials Used

cells.Teacher's Activities: i. Teacher identifies and displays materials used for skin care (soap, sponge, towel, body cream, hair cream). ii.Teacher names each material clearly and repeatedly. iii. Teacher demonstrates use of each material. iv. Teacher guides pupils to identify materials. v. Teacher plays identification games with materials.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i. Pupils identify materials used to take care of the skin. ii.Pupils point to each material when named. iii.Pupils touch and hold materials safely. iv.Pupils match materials to their uses. v. Pupils participate in "Find the..." games.
cells.Learning Resources: Soap Sponge Towel Body cream Hair cream Charts Pictures Sorting baskets

cells.Teacher's Activities: Assessment through observation: Teacher observes pupils' ability to identify body parts, skin care materials, and demonstrate simple bathing actions
cells.Pupil's Activities: Pupils demonstrate simple hygiene actions, identify materials, and participate in assessment activities
cells.Learning Resources: Assessment sheets All materials for demonstration

cells.Teacher's Activities: Rest and relaxation period
cells.Pupil's Activities: Rest and relaxation

weeks.topic:
Care of the Mouth
and Teeth I - Introduction

cells.Teacher's Activities:
i. Teacher uses charts and large teeth model
to introduce teeth and mouth. ii.Teacher lets pupils look at their teeth in mirrors. iii.Teacher sings teeth songs ("Brush, brush, brush your teeth"). iv.Teacher shows pictures of healthy teeth vs unhealthy teeth. v. Teacher explains teeth help us eat food.
cells.Pupil's Activities:
i. Pupils point to their mouth and
teeth. ii.Pupils look at teeth in mirrors. iii. Pupils sing teeth songs. iv.Pupils identify healthy teeth in pictures. v. Pupils mime chewing food.
cells.Learning Resources:
Large teeth model
Mirrors Charts Pictures Video clips Posters

weeks.topic: Care of the Mouth and Teeth II - Brushing Twice Daily

cells.Teacher's Activities: i. Teacher demonstrates brushing teeth using large teeth model and toothbrush. ii. Teacher emphasizes brushing in the morning and at night. iii.Teacher acts out morning and bedtime brushing routine. iv.Teacher uses pictures showing "morning" (sun) and "night" (moon). v. Teacher guides pupils to mime brushing.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i. Pupils watch brushing demonstration. ii. Pupils identify morning and night pictures. iii.Pupils mime brushing teeth. iv.Pupils count "one, two" for twice daily. v. Pupils sing brushing song with actions.
cells.Learning Resources: Large teeth model Toothbrush Charts Sun/moon pictures Video clips Sequence cards

weeks.topic: Care of the Mouth and Teeth III - Using Mouthwash

cells.Teacher's Activities:
i. Teacher shows mouthwash bottle and explains its use in very simple terms. ii. Teacher demonstrates rinsing mouth with water (mouthwash practice should be supervised by parents). iii.Teacher shows pictures of clean
mouth. iv.Teacher emphasizes asking parents for help with mouthwash. v. Teacher practices rinsing and spitting actions.
cells.Pupil's Activities:
i.Pupils identify mouthwash bottle. ii. Pupils mime rinsing their mouth. iii.Pupils practice spitting actions (without liquid). iv. Pupils understand to ask parents for help. v. Pupils participate
in mouth care routine.
cells.Learning Resources: Mouthwash bottle (for display) Cup Water Charts Pictures Video clips

weeks.topic: Care of the Mouth and Teeth IV - Materials Used

cells.Teacher's Activities: i.Teacher identifies and displays all mouth care materials (toothbrush, toothpaste, mouthwash, cup). ii. Teacher names each material clearly. iii.Teacher demonstrates complete mouth care routine. iv.Teacher guides pupils to identify each material. v. Teacher plays matching games with materials.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i.Pupils identify materials needed to take care of mouth and teeth. ii.Pupils point to materials when named. iii.Pupils demonstrate complete brushing routine. iv. Pupils match materials to pictures. v. Pupils sort dental care items.
cells.Learning Resources: Toothbrush Toothpaste Mouthwash Cup Charts Pictures Toy dental sets

cells.Teacher's Activities: Teacher reviews all first term topics using songs, games, and demonstrations. Reviews body parts, skin care (bathing, cream, materials), and mouth care (brushing, materials).
cells.Pupil's Activities: Pupils sing health songs, demonstrate bathing and brushing actions, identify all materials learned, participate in review games.
cells.Learning Resources: All materials from weeks 1- 10 Charts Pictures Games

cells.Teacher's Activities: End of term assessment through observation and demonstration of all hygiene practices learned
cells.Pupil's Activities: Pupils demonstrate skin care and mouth care routines, identify all materials, show understanding through actions
cells.Learning Resources: Assessment materials All demonstration items

cells.Teacher's Activities: Teacher distributes progress reports, gives praise and encouragement, assigns simple holiday practice (brush teeth, take bath daily)
cells.Pupil's Activities: Pupils receive reports, simple awards/stickers for participation, celebrate their learning
cells.Learning Resources: Reports Certificates Stickers Treats

cells.Teacher's Activities: i.Teacher revises first term work using songs and demonstrations. ii.Teacher reviews body parts, skin care, and mouth care. iii.Teacher uses quick demonstrations with dolls. iv. Teacher assesses retention through simple questions and actions.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i.Pupils participate in revision activities. ii.Pupils sing familiar health songs. iii.Pupils demonstrate bathing and brushing. iv. Pupils identify materials from first term.
cells.Learning Resources: All previous materials Charts Pictures Dolls Video clips

cells.Teacher's Activities: i. Teacher explains "environment" as "the place around us" in very simple terms. ii.Teacher points to things in the classroom environment. iii.Teacher takes pupils on a simple tour of school environment. iv.Teacher uses pictures of different environments (home, school, playground). v. Teacher introduces "clean" and "dirty" concepts with pictures.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i.Pupils look around their classroom. ii. Pupils point to things in their environment. iii. Pupils walk around and observe. iv.Pupils identify pictures of different places. v. Pupils begin to understand clean vs dirty.
cells.Learning Resources: Pictures of environments Charts Posters Real classroom Video clips

cells.Teacher's Activities:
i. Teacher shows clear pictures of clean environments and dirty environments.
ii. Teacher uses "clean" and "dirty" flashcards. iii. Teacher shows video clips of clean and dirty places. iv.Teacher guides pupils to say "clean" or "dirty" for each picture. v. Teacher uses happy face for clean, sad face for dirty.
cells.Pupil's Activities:
i.Pupils look at pictures carefully. ii. Pupils say "clean" or "dirty" with
guidance. iii.Pupils point to clean environments. iv. Pupils point to dirty environments. v. Pupils make happy/sad faces accordingly.
cells.Learning Resources:
Pictures Flashcards Video clips Happy/sad
face cards Charts Posters

cells.Teacher's Activities: i.Teacher uses charts and pictures to show things in clean environments (organized toys, clean floors, neat tables, flowers, trash in bins). ii.Teacher points out clean things in the classroom. iii.Teacher shows pictures of clean homes, schools, and playgrounds. iv. Teacher emphasizes "everything in its place." v. Teacher lets pupils identify clean things.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i.Pupils list simple things found in clean environment (with guidance). ii.Pupils point to clean areas in classroom. iii.Pupils identify organized vs messy pictures. iv.Pupils clap for clean environments. v. Pupils touch clean, neat objects.
cells.Learning Resources: Charts Pictures Video clips Classroom items Posters Clean environment photos

cells.Teacher's Activities: Assessment through observation: Teacher assesses pupils' understanding of clean vs dirty environments and identification of clean things
cells.Pupil's Activities: Pupils identify clean and dirty pictures, demonstrate understanding of environment concepts
cells.Learning Resources: Assessment materials Pictures Charts

cells.Teacher's Activities:
Rest and relaxation
period
cells.Pupil's Activities: Rest and relaxation

weeks.topic: Clean Environment II - How to Make Environment Clean

cells.Teacher's Activities: i. Teacher demonstrates picking up toys and putting them in boxes. ii.Teacher shows how to put trash in waste bins. iii.Teacher demonstrates simple sweeping with toy broom. iv.Teacher shows pictures of children cleaning up. v. Teacher involves pupils in classroom cleanup activity.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i. Pupils watch cleaning demonstrations. ii. Pupils pick up toys and put them away. iii.Pupils put trash in bins. iv.Pupils practice with toy cleaning tools. v. Pupils help clean classroom with guidance.
cells.Learning Resources: Toy broom Dustpan Waste bin Toys Cleaning cloths Pictures Charts

cells.Teacher's Activities: i.Teacher identifies and displays cleaning materials (broom, dustpan, waste bin, duster, cleaning cloth). ii. Teacher names each material clearly and repeatedly. iii.Teacher demonstrates safe use of each material. iv.Teacher emphasizes putting things in the waste bin. v. Teacher guides pupils to identify materials.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i.Pupils identify materials needed to keep environment clean. ii.Pupils point to each material when named. iii.Pupils touch and hold cleaning tools safely. iv.Pupils mime sweeping and cleaning actions. v. Pupils practice putting things away.
cells.Learning Resources: Broom Dustpan Waste bin Duster Cleaning cloth Charts Pictures

cells.Teacher's Activities:
i. Teacher shows pictures of dirty environments (trash on floor, scattered toys, dirty surfaces, messy areas). ii. Teacher uses
sad/unhappy faces to show dirty is not good. iii. Teacher shows real examples of messy areas (safely controlled). iv. Teacher guides pupils to identify dirty things. v. Teacher emphasizes we should not make places dirty.
cells.Pupil's Activities:
i. Pupils identify things found in dirty environments (with guidance). ii.Pupils point to messy/dirty pictures. iii. Pupils make sad
faces for dirty places. iv.Pupils shake heads "no" for dirty environments. v. Pupils understand dirty is not good.
cells.Learning Resources: Pictures of dirty places Charts Video clips Sad face cards Posters

weeks.topic: Dirty Environment - How to Make it Clean

cells.Teacher's Activities: i.Teacher demonstrates transforming dirty area to clean area. ii.Teacher shows before and after pictures. iii. Teacher involves pupils in cleaning messy corner of classroom. iv. Teacher demonstrates complete cleanup process step by step. v. Teacher praises pupils for making environment clean.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i.Pupils watch transformation demonstration. ii.Pupils identify before and after pictures. iii.Pupils participate in cleanup activity. iv.Pupils pick up scattered items. v. Pupils understand making dirty places clean.
cells.Learning Resources: Before/after pictures Cleaning materials Messy items to clean Charts Waste bin

cells.Teacher's Activities: Teacher reviews all second term topics: environment concepts, clean vs dirty, things in clean/dirty environments, cleaning materials and methods.
cells.Pupil's Activities: Pupils demonstrate understanding of clean and dirty environments, identify cleaning materials, participate in cleanup activities, sing environment songs.
cells.Learning Resources: All materials from second term Charts Pictures Cleaning tools

cells.Teacher's Activities:
End of term assessment of
environment awareness and cleaning practices
cells.Pupil's Activities:
Pupils identify clean and dirty
environments, demonstrate cleaning actions, identify materials used for cleaning
cells.Learning Resources:
Assessment materials
Pictures Cleaning tools

cells.Teacher's Activities: Distribution of reports, feedback, encouragement to keep environments clean during holidays
cells.Pupil's Activities: Pupils receive reports, recognition for participation, celebrate environmental awareness
cells.Learning Resources: Reports Certificates Stickers

cells.Teacher's Activities: i.Teacher comprehensively revises first and second term topics. ii.Teacher uses songs, games, and demonstrations. iii.Teacher reviews skin care, mouth care, and environment. iv. Teacher assesses retention and reinforces key concepts.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i.Pupils participate actively in revision. ii.Pupils demonstrate all hygiene practices learned. iii. Pupils identify materials from previous terms. iv. Pupils show understanding of clean environment.
cells.Learning Resources: All previous materials Charts Pictures Videos Dolls

weeks.topic: Clean and Dirty Environments - Causes of Dirty Environment

cells.Teacher's Activities: i. Teacher shows pictures of actions that make environment dirty (throwing trash on floor, spilling things, not putting toys away). ii.Teacher demonstrates "wrong" actions and says "No, no." iii. Teacher shows video clips of littering and messiness. iv.Teacher explains these cause dirty environment in simple terms. v. Teacher emphasizes not doing these things.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i. Pupils identify actions that make places dirty. ii.Pupils shake heads "no" for bad actions. iii.Pupils understand throwing trash is wrong. iv. Pupils recognize causes of mess. v. Pupils say "no" to dirty actions.
cells.Learning Resources: Pictures Video clips Charts Before/after photos Posters

weeks.topic:
Clean and Dirty Environments -
Effects and Importance

cells.Teacher's Activities:
i. Teacher shows effects of dirty
environment (flies, bad smell, sickness, ugly places) using pictures. ii.Teacher shows importance of clean environment (healthy, beautiful, happy, safe) using pictures. iii.Teacher uses happy children in clean places vs sad faces in dirty places. iv.Teacher emphasizes clean is good, dirty is bad in very simple terms. v. Teacher praises clean habits.
cells.Pupil's Activities:
i. Pupils identify happy children in
clean places. ii.Pupils understand clean environment is good. iii. Pupils make happy faces for clean places. iv.Pupils understand dirty can make us sick. v. Pupils prefer clean environments.
cells.Learning Resources:
Pictures Charts
Happy/sad faces Video clips Posters Health images

cells.Teacher's Activities: i. Teacher explains "personal hygiene" as "keeping our body clean" in very simple terms. ii. Teacher shows pictures of clean, well- groomed children. iii.Teacher reviews all hygiene practices learned (bathing, brushing teeth, clean clothes). iv.Teacher emphasizes importance (healthy, look good, feel good, no germs). v. Teacher uses songs about being clean.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i. Pupils understand personal hygiene means clean body. ii.Pupils identify clean, neat children in pictures. iii.Pupils list hygiene practices with guidance. iv.Pupils understand being clean is important. v. Pupils sing cleanliness songs.
cells.Learning Resources: Pictures of groomed children Charts Video clips Posters Dolls

cells.Teacher's Activities:
Assessment of understanding of causes/effects of dirty environment and personal hygiene
concepts
cells.Pupil's Activities:
Pupils demonstrate understanding of environmental concepts and personal hygiene
importance
cells.Learning Resources: Assessment materials Pictures Charts

cells.Teacher's Activities: Rest and relaxation period
cells.Pupil's Activities: Rest and relaxation

weeks.topic: Personal Hygiene - How to Maintain Good Personal Hygiene

cells.Teacher's Activities: i.Teacher demonstrates complete daily hygiene routine (wake up, wash face, brush teeth, bathe, wear clean clothes, comb hair, wash hands). ii. Teacher uses picture sequence cards showing daily routine. iii.Teacher involves pupils in role-play of hygiene routine. iv.Teacher emphasizes doing these things every day. v. Teacher reviews all hygiene materials.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i.Pupils watch complete hygiene demonstration. ii.Pupils arrange sequence cards with help. iii.Pupils role-play daily hygiene routine. iv.Pupils mime all hygiene actions. v. Pupils demonstrate good personal hygiene.
cells.Learning Resources: Sequence cards All hygiene materials Dolls Pictures Charts Video clips

cells.Teacher's Activities: i.Teacher explains "good health" as "feeling strong and well" in simple terms. ii.Teacher shows pictures of healthy, active children vs sick children. iii.Teacher asks pupils to show strong arms/muscles. iv.Teacher uses happy, energetic actions to show good health. v. Teacher emphasizes being healthy is wonderful.
cells.Pupil's Activities: i.Pupils understand good health means feeling well. ii.Pupils identify healthy children in pictures. iii. Pupils show their strong arms/muscles. iv.Pupils jump, run (safely) to show they are healthy. v. Pupils make happy faces for good health.
cells.Learning Resources: Pictures of healthy children Charts Video clips Posters

cells.Teacher's Activities:
i. Teacher shows pictures of good,
nutritious food (fruits, vegetables, rice, beans, fish, eggs, milk). ii.Teacher explains good food makes us strong and healthy. iii.Teacher shows clean food vs dirty food. iv.Teacher lets pupils identify healthy foods. v. Teacher emphasizes eating good food every day.
cells.Pupil's Activities:
i. Pupils identify good, healthy foods.
ii. Pupils point to fruits and vegetables. iii. Pupils understand good food helps us grow. iv.Pupils mime eating good food. v. Pupils choose healthy food pictures.
cells.Learning Resources:

The teacher takes pupils on a nature walk around the school compound to observe plants. ii.The teacher explains that plants are living things that grow in soil and need water and sunlight. iii. The teacher shows real plants and pictures of different plants. iv.The teacher demonstrates how to touch plants gently. Identification Activities: i. The teacher points out different parts of plants (leaves, stem, roots, flowers). ii. The teacher names various plants in the environment. iii.The teacher shows pictures and real samples of common plants. Examples:
i. The teacher presents examples: flowers (rose, sunflower), grass, trees (mango tree, palm tree). ii.The teacher uses picture cards to show variety of plants. iii. The teacher sings plant-related songs.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Learning Activities: i. Pupils observe plants during nature walk. ii.Pupils listen and repeat "plants are living things" iii.Pupils look at and touch real plants gently. iv.Pupils observe plant parts pointed out by teacher. Identification: i.Pupils point to plants around them. ii.Pupils name plants they see (with teacher's help). iii.Pupils identify plants in pictures. Examples: i.Pupils look at different plant examples. ii. Pupils match picture cards of plants. iii. Pupils sing plant songs with
actions.
cells.MATERIALS: Real plants (potted) Picture cards of plants Chart showing parts of plants Flowers Grass samples Leaves Song charts Nature walk area

weeks.topic: LIVING THINGS: PLANTS (Continued) - Growing plants - Caring for plants - Drawing and coloring plants

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Plant Care: i.The teacher demonstrates how to water plants properly. ii.The teacher explains that plants need water, sunlight, and soil to grow. iii.The teacher shows pupils how to care for classroom plants. iv. The teacher discusses what happens when plants don't get water (they die). Hands-on Activities: i. The teacher guides pupils in planting seeds in small pots or cups. ii. The teacher demonstrates gentle handling of plants. iii. The teacher organizes plant watering activities.
Creative Activities: i. The teacher provides plant pictures for coloring. ii.The teacher guides pupils in drawing simple plants. iii. The teacher uses stickers and craft materials for plant activities.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Plant Care: i.Pupils watch watering demonstration. ii. Pupils understand plants need water and sunlight. iii. Pupils help water classroom plants (with supervision). iv.Pupils observe healthy and unhealthy plants. Hands-on: i.Pupils plant seeds in small containers. ii.Pupils handle plants gently. iii. Pupils take turns watering plants. Creative: i.Pupils color plant pictures. ii. Pupils draw
simple plants (flowers, trees). iii. Pupils create plant crafts with teacher's guidance.
cells.MATERIALS: Small pots/cups Soil Seeds (beans, maize) Watering can Real plants Coloring sheets Crayons Drawing paper Plant stickers Craft materials

weeks.topic: LIVING THINGS: FRUITS - Meaning of fruits - Identification of fruits - Examples of fruits - Fruits come from plants

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Introduction to Fruits: i. The teacher explains that fruits are parts of plants that we can eat. ii. The teacher shows real fruits (apple, banana, orange, mango). iii.The teacher allows pupils to touch, smell, and observe fruits. iv.The teacher explains that fruits come from plants/trees. Identification: i.The teacher displays various fruits and names each one. ii.The teacher describes fruits by color, shape, and size. iii.The teacher uses picture cards for
fruit recognition. iv. The teacher cuts fruits to show inside (seeds, flesh). Activities: i.The teacher organizes fruit tasting activity (with permission). ii.The teacher plays fruit identification games. iii. The teacher teaches fruit-related songs and rhymes.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Learning: i.Pupils learn that fruits come from plants. ii.Pupils observe real fruits brought by teacher. iii. Pupils touch, smell, and feel different fruits. iv. Pupils understand fruits grow on plants. Identification: i.Pupils identify and name different fruits. ii. Pupils describe fruits (red apple, yellow banana). iii.Pupils match fruit pictures. iv.Pupils observe cut fruits and seeds.
Activities: i.Pupils taste different fruits (if permitted). ii.Pupils play fruit games. iii. Pupils sing fruit songs enthusiastically.
cells.MATERIALS: Real fruits (apple, banana, orange, mango, pineapple) Fruit pictures Flashcards Chart showing fruits Cutting board and knife (teacher use) Plates Fruit song charts Fruit models/toys

weeks.topic: ANIMALS - Meaning of animals -Description of animals -Parts of animal bodies - Similarities between animals and humans

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Introduction to Animals: i. The teacher explains that animals are living things that can move from place to place. ii.The teacher shows pictures and toy animals. iii. The teacher describes different animals (dog, cat, goat, cow, bird, fish). iv. The teacher makes animal sounds and encourages imitation. Body Parts: i. The teacher identifies animal body parts: head, eyes, ears, nose, mouth, legs, tail.
ii. The teacher compares animal parts with human parts. iii.The teacher shows that both animals and humans have eyes, ears, nose, mouth. iv.The teacher discusses differences (tails, four legs vs two legs). Activities: i.The teacher plays animal movement games (hop like a rabbit, walk like a dog). ii.The teacher uses videos or pictures showing animals. iii. The teacher sings animal songs.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Learning: i.Pupils understand animals are living things. ii.Pupils observe animal pictures and toys. iii. Pupils listen to descriptions of animals. iv.Pupils make animal sounds (moo, bark, meow). Body Parts: i.Pupils identify animal body parts in pictures. ii. Pupils point to their own body parts (like animals). iii.Pupils understand similarities: we
both have eyes, ears, etc. iv. Pupils notice differences: animals have tails, four legs. Activities: i.Pupils imitate animal movements. ii. Pupils watch animal videos/pictures. iii. Pupils sing animal songs with actions.
cells.MATERIALS: Animal pictures Toy animals Animal flashcards Chart showing animal body parts Videos of animals (optional) Animal masks Song charts Story books about animals

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Assessment Activities: i. The teacher administers comprehensive pre- science assessment. ii.The teacher tests knowledge of plants (identification, parts). iii.The teacher assesses fruit recognition and naming. iv. The teacher tests animal identification and sounds. v. The teacher
evaluates understanding of body parts (animals and humans). vi.The teacher uses oral questions, picture identification, and practical tasks. vii.The teacher observes pupils' responses and participation. viii. The teacher records individual performance and identifies areas needing support.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Assessment Tasks: i. Pupils identify plants in pictures and real samples. ii.Pupils name parts of plants shown. iii.Pupils identify and name fruits presented. iv.Pupils identify animals in pictures. v.Pupils make animal sounds when asked.
vi. Pupils point to animal body parts. vii. Pupils identify their own body parts. viii. Pupils demonstrate understanding of topics covered.
cells.MATERIALS: Assessment sheets Plant samples Fruit pictures Animal pictures Body parts chart Real objects Mark book Assessment checklist

weeks.topic: DOMESTIC ANIMALS -Meaning of domestic animals - Examples of domestic animals -Where domestic animals live - Caring for domestic animals

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Introduction: i.The teacher explains that domestic animals are animals we keep at home. ii.The teacher lists examples: dog, cat, rabbit, chicken, goat, sheep, cow. iii. The teacher shows pictures of domestic animals. iv.The teacher discusses why we keep these animals at home (pets, food, help). Homes of Animals: i. The teacher shows where domestic animals live (kennel for dogs, coop for
chickens). ii.The teacher discusses how we care for domestic animals (feeding, cleaning, shelter). iii.The teacher demonstrates responsible animal care. Activities: i.The teacher organizes visit to see domestic animals (if possible). ii.The teacher plays domestic animal identification games. iii. The teacher teaches songs about domestic animals.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Learning: i.Pupils understand domestic animals live with us. ii.Pupils name domestic animals: dog, cat, chicken, goat. iii.Pupils observe pictures of domestic animals. iv. Pupils learn we keep them for various reasons. Animal Homes: i. Pupils identify where animals live (kennel, coop).
ii. Pupils understand animals need food and care. iii.Pupils learn to treat animals kindly. Activities: i.Pupils observe domestic animals (if available). ii. Pupils play animal identification games. iii. Pupils sing songs about domestic animals with enthusiasm.
cells.MATERIALS: Pictures of domestic animals Toy domestic animals Pictures of animal homes Flashcards Chart showing domestic animals Song charts Story books Videos (optional)

weeks.topic: PARTS OF THE BODY: THE HEAD -Identification of the head - Parts on the head - Uses of the head

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Introduction to the Head: i. The teacher points to their own head and asks pupils to touch theirs. ii. The teacher explains the head is the top part of our body. iii.The teacher shows pictures and charts of the head. iv.The teacher names parts found on the head: hair, forehead, eyes, ears, nose, mouth, chin.
Parts on the Head: i.The teacher identifies each part on their own head. ii.The teacher asks pupils to point to each part on their own heads. iii. The teacher uses a large diagram showing parts of the head. iv. The teacher plays "Simon Says" touching head parts. Uses of the Head: i.The teacher explains: the head holds our brain (for thinking), face (for seeing, smelling, eating, hearing). ii.The teacher demonstrates nodding (yes) and shaking head (no). iii. The teacher discusses protecting our heads (wearing helmets).
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Learning: i.Pupils touch their own heads. ii.Pupils understand the head is on top of the body. iii.Pupils observe head pictures and charts. iv.Pupils identify parts on the head. Parts Identification: i. Pupils point to their hair, eyes, ears, nose,
mouth. ii.Pupils touch each part when named by teacher. iii. Pupils observe large head diagram. iv.Pupils play "Simon Says" game with head parts. Uses: i.Pupils understand the head helps us think, see, hear, smell, eat. ii.Pupils practice nodding and shaking head. iii. Pupils learn to protect their heads.
cells.MATERIALS: Large body chart Head diagram Mirror Pictures of heads Flashcards Helmet (for demonstration) Simon Says game materials

weeks.topic:
PARTS OF THE BODY: MOUTH AND TEETH -Identification of the mouth - Identification of the teeth -Uses of mouth and teeth - Care of mouth and
teeth

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
The Mouth: i.The teacher points to their mouth and asks pupils to point to theirs. ii.The teacher shows pictures of mouths. iii. The teacher opens mouth to show inside: teeth,
tongue, gums. iv. The teacher uses a mirror so pupils can see their own mouths. The Teeth: i.The teacher identifies teeth inside the mouth. ii.The teacher explains teeth help us chew food. iii.The teacher shows picture of healthy teeth. iv.The teacher discusses baby teeth and adult teeth (simply). Uses and Care: i.The teacher explains: mouth is for eating, talking, singing, drinking. ii. The teacher explains: teeth are for biting and chewing food. iii. The teacher demonstrates proper tooth brushing. iv.The teacher emphasizes brushing teeth twice daily. v. The teacher discusses healthy foods for strong teeth.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
The Mouth: i.Pupils point to their mouths. ii.Pupils observe mouth pictures. iii.Pupils open their mouths to see teeth and tongue. iv.Pupils look at their mouths
in mirrors. The Teeth: i.Pupils identify their teeth. ii.Pupils understand teeth help us chew. iii.Pupils observe pictures of teeth. iv. Pupils count some of their teeth (with help). Uses and Care: i.Pupils understand mouth is for eating and talking. ii.Pupils understand teeth help us chew food. iii. Pupils watch tooth brushing demonstration. iv.Pupils practice brushing motion. v. Pupils learn to brush teeth daily.
cells.MATERIALS: Mirrors Pictures of mouth and teeth Toothbrush and toothpaste Dental chart Flashcards Healthy food pictures Tooth brushing song chart

weeks.topic:
PARTS OF THE BODY: LIPS AND TONGUE
- Identification of lips -Identification of tongue -Uses of lips and tongue - Importance of these organs

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
The Lips: i. The teacher points to their lips
and asks pupils to touch theirs. ii.The teacher explains lips are the outer part of the mouth. iii.The teacher shows that lips can move (smiling, pouting, talking). iv. The teacher uses pictures showing lips. The Tongue: i.The teacher sticks out tongue and asks pupils to see theirs in mirror. ii.The teacher explains the tongue is inside the mouth. iii.The teacher shows pictures of the tongue. iv.The teacher demonstrates tongue movements. Uses: i.The teacher explains: lips help us talk, eat, drink, whistle, kiss, smile. ii.The teacher explains: tongue helps us taste food, talk, swallow, lick. iii.The teacher discusses how we taste different flavors (sweet, sour, bitter, salty). iv.The teacher conducts simple tasting activity (if
permitted). v. The teacher emphasizes keeping lips and tongue clean.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
The Lips: i. Pupils touch their lips.
ii. Pupils understand lips are outside the mouth. iii.Pupils move their lips (smile, pout). iv.Pupils observe lip pictures. The Tongue: i.Pupils stick out their tongues safely. ii.Pupils see their tongues in mirrors. iii.Pupils observe tongue pictures. iv.Pupils move their tongues around. Uses: i.Pupils understand lips help us talk and eat. ii. Pupils understand tongue helps us taste food. iii.Pupils learn about different tastes. iv.Pupils taste safe foods (if permitted). v. Pupils learn to keep mouth parts clean.
cells.MATERIALS:
Mirrors Pictures of lips and tongue
Body parts chart Safe tasting samples (sugar- sweet, lemon- sour) Flashcards Song charts about body parts

weeks.topic: REVISION OF FIRST TERM WORK All topics covered

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Comprehensive Revision: i. The teacher systematically reviews living things: plants (identification, parts, care). ii. The teacher revises fruits (identification, examples, where they come from). iii. The teacher reviews animals (meaning, body parts, similarities with humans). iv. The teacher revises domestic animals (examples, where they live, care). v. The teacher reviews parts of the body: head, mouth, teeth, lips, tongue. vi.The teacher revises uses of each body part. vii.The teacher uses games, songs, and interactive activities for revision. viii.The teacher conducts mock examination activities. ix. The teacher
identifies areas where pupils need extra support. x. The teacher builds confidence for final examination.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Revision Activities: i. Pupils identify plants and their parts. ii.Pupils name and identify various fruits. iii.Pupils identify animals and their body parts. iv.Pupils name domestic animals and their uses. v. Pupils identify all body parts learned: head, mouth, teeth, lips, tongue. vi.Pupils explain uses of body parts (with help). vii.Pupils participate in revision games and songs. viii.Pupils complete mock test activities. ix.Pupils ask questions about difficult areas. x. Pupils prepare confidently for
examination.
cells.MATERIALS: All term's materials Plant samples Fruit pictures Animal pictures Body parts charts Revision worksheets Mock test materials Games Song charts

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Examination Administration: i. The teacher administers comprehensive end- of-term examination. ii.The teacher tests plant identification and knowledge. iii.The teacher assesses fruit recognition and naming. iv. The teacher tests animal knowledge (identification, sounds, body parts). v. The teacher assesses domestic animal knowledge. vi. The teacher tests body parts identification (head, mouth, teeth, lips, tongue). vii. The teacher evaluates understanding of uses of body parts. viii. The teacher uses oral questions, picture identification, and practical demonstrations. ix.The teacher marks examination
and records scores. x. The teacher prepares report cards with comments.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Examination Tasks: i. Pupils identify plants in pictures and real samples. ii. Pupils name fruits shown in pictures. iii. Pupils identify animals and make appropriate sounds. iv. Pupils name domestic animals. v.Pupils point to and name body parts: head, mouth, teeth, lips, tongue. vi.Pupils explain uses of body parts (simply). vii.Pupils answer oral questions from teacher. viii.Pupils demonstrate practical knowledge. ix. Pupils complete all examination
tasks. x. Pupils show understanding of first term topics.
cells.MATERIALS: Examination materials Plant pictures Fruit pictures Animal pictures Body parts chart Real samples Assessment sheets Mark book Report cards

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES: Closing Activities: i.The teacher returns marked examination scripts. ii.The teacher discusses individual performance with pupils. iii.The teacher celebrates pupils' science learning achievements. iv.The teacher awards certificates/stickers for good performance. v.The teacher distributes report cards. vi.The teacher provides holiday tips (observing plants, animals at home). vii.The teacher gives preview of second term topics. viii. The teacher encourages continued observation of nature. ix. The teacher thanks pupils for active participation.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES: Closing Activities: i. Pupils receive marked work and report cards. ii. Pupils listen to teacher's feedback. iii.Pupils celebrate their science learning. iv.Pupils receive awards and recognition. v.Pupils get holiday observation tasks. vi.Pupils look forward to second term. vii. Pupils say goodbye to classmates and teacher.
cells.MATERIALS: Report cards Marked scripts Certificates Awards/stickers Holiday observation sheets Celebration materials

weeks.topic: THE FIVE SENSES: Introduction - What are senses? -The five senses overview - Sense organs introduction

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Introduction to Senses: i. The teacher welcomes pupils back and reviews first term briefly. ii.The teacher explains that senses help us know about things around us. iii.The teacher introduces the five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste, touch. iv. The teacher shows pictures of the five sense organs. Sense Organs: i.The teacher names sense organs: eyes (seeing), ears (hearing), nose (smelling), tongue (tasting), skin (touching). ii. The teacher asks pupils to point to each organ on their bodies. iii.The teacher explains each sense helps us in different ways. Activities: i.The teacher sings "Five Senses Song" ii.The teacher plays identification games
with senses. iii. The teacher uses charts showing the five senses.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Learning: i.Pupils understand senses help us know things. ii.Pupils learn there are five senses. iii.Pupils observe pictures of sense organs. Identification: i.Pupils point to their eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and touch their skin. ii.Pupils name sense organs with teacher. iii.Pupils understand each sense does something different. Activities: i.Pupils sing five senses song. ii.Pupils participate in sense games. iii. Pupils observe and discuss sense
charts.
cells.MATERIALS: Five senses chart Pictures of sense organs Body diagram Flashcards Song charts Story books about senses

weeks.topic: THE SENSE OF SIGHT: EYES -The eyes as organs of sight - Uses of eyes - Caring for our eyes

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
The Eyes: i.The teacher explains eyes help us see things around us. ii.The teacher asks pupils to point to their eyes. iii.The teacher shows pictures of eyes and explains parts (eyelids, eyelashes, eyebrows). iv. The teacher uses mirrors so pupils can see their own eyes. Uses of Eyes: i.The teacher explains: eyes help us see colors, shapes, people, things, words, pictures. ii. The teacher demonstrates looking at various objects. iii.The teacher plays "I Spy" game using sight. iv.The teacher discusses what happens when we close our eyes (can't see). Eye Care: i. The teacher teaches: don't rub eyes with dirty hands, don't look at bright sun, visit eye doctor, eat healthy
foods (carrots), rest eyes when tired. ii.The teacher demonstrates proper face washing including eyes. iii. The teacher discusses wearing glasses if needed.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
The Eyes: i.Pupils understand eyes help us see. ii.Pupils point to their eyes. iii. Pupils observe eye pictures. iv. Pupils look at their eyes in mirrors. Uses: i.Pupils understand eyes help us see everything around us. ii.Pupils look at objects teacher points out. iii. Pupils play "I Spy" using their sight. iv. Pupils experience closing eyes and not seeing. Care: i.Pupils learn to keep hands away from eyes. ii.Pupils learn not to look at bright sun. iii. Pupils
understand importance of eye health. iv. Pupils learn about healthy foods for eyes.
cells.MATERIALS: Mirrors Eye pictures and charts Various colorful objects Pictures of healthy foods Glasses (for demonstration) I Spy game materials Eye care posters

weeks.topic: THE SENSE OF HEARING: EARS & THE SENSE OF SMELL: NOSE -Ears as organs of hearing -Nose as organ of smell - Uses and care

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
The Ears: i.The teacher explains ears help us hear sounds. ii. The teacher asks pupils to touch their ears. iii.The teacher makes different sounds (clapping, bell, whistle) for pupils to hear. iv.The teacher shows pictures of ears. Uses and Care of Ears: i. The teacher explains: ears help us hear voices, music, warnings, animals, nature sounds. ii.The teacher teaches: don't put things in ears, keep ears clean, protect from loud noise. iii.The teacher plays listening games. The Nose: i.The teacher explains nose helps us smell things. ii.The teacher asks pupils to touch their
noses. iii.The teacher presents items with different smells (perfume, orange, soap). iv.The teacher guides safe smelling activities. Uses and Care: i.The teacher explains: nose helps us smell good and bad things, helps us breathe. ii.The teacher teaches: blow nose gently with tissue, keep nose clean. iii. The teacher plays smell identification games (if safe).
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
The Ears: i.Pupils understand ears help us hear. ii.Pupils touch their ears. iii.Pupils listen to different sounds made by teacher. iv. Pupils observe ear pictures. Care: i.Pupils understand ears help us hear many things. ii. Pupils learn to keep ears safe and clean. iii.Pupils play listening games. The Nose: i.Pupils understand nose helps us smell. ii.Pupils touch their noses. iii. Pupils smell
different safe items. iv. Pupils practice safe smelling. Care: i.Pupils understand nose helps us breathe and smell. ii.Pupils learn to keep nose clean. iii. Pupils identify smells in games.
cells.MATERIALS: Pictures of ears and nose Sound-making objects (bell, drum, whistle) Safe smelling items (perfume, orange, flower, soap) Tissues Body charts Listening game materials

weeks.topic: THE SENSE OF TOUCH: SKIN & THE SENSE OF TASTE: TONGUE -Skin as organ of touch - Tongue as organ of taste - Uses and care

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
The Skin (Touch): i.The teacher explains skin covers our whole body and helps us feel. ii. The teacher asks pupils to touch their skin (arms, face, hands). iii.The teacher presents objects with different textures (soft, hard, rough, smooth, hot, cold). iv.The teacher guides touching activities safely. Uses and Care: i. The teacher explains: skin helps us feel things,
protects our body, shows when something is hot or sharp. ii. The teacher teaches: keep skin clean (bathing), use lotion, protect from sun, cover wounds. The Tongue (Taste): i.The teacher reviews tongue from first term. ii.The teacher explains tongue helps us taste flavors. iii. The teacher introduces four basic tastes: sweet, sour, salty, bitter. iv.The teacher provides safe tasting samples (if permitted). Uses and Care: i.The teacher explains: tongue helps us taste food, talk, swallow. ii. The teacher teaches: keep mouth clean, brush teeth, don't eat dirty things.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
The Skin: i.Pupils understand skin helps us feel. ii. Pupils touch their skin on different body parts. iii.Pupils touch objects with different textures. iv.Pupils identify soft, hard, rough, smooth objects. Care: i. Pupils understand skin protects us
and helps us feel. ii.Pupils learn to keep skin clean and safe. iii.Pupils understand importance of bathing. The Tongue: i.Pupils recall tongue from first term. ii.Pupils understand tongue helps us taste. iii.Pupils learn about sweet, sour, salty, bitter. iv. Pupils taste safe foods (if permitted). Care: i.Pupils understand multiple uses of tongue. ii. Pupils learn to keep mouth and tongue clean.
cells.MATERIALS: Different textured objects (cotton, sandpaper, stone, fabric) Body diagram Safe tasting samples (if permitted) Soap and water Lotion Pictures of skin care Taste flashcards

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Assessment Activities: i. The teacher administers mid-term assessment on the five senses. ii.The teacher tests identification of sense organs (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin).
iii. The teacher assesses understanding of what each sense does. iv. The teacher tests matching senses to their uses. v.The teacher evaluates knowledge of sense organ care. vi.The teacher uses oral questions and practical demonstrations. vii. The teacher assesses through games (listening, smelling, touching, seeing activities). viii. The teacher records pupils' performance.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Assessment Tasks: i. Pupils identify all five sense organs on their bodies. ii.Pupils name what each sense organ does (eyes-see,
ears-hear, nose- smell, tongue- taste, skin- touch). iii.Pupils match senses to activities. iv.Pupils demonstrate understanding of sense organ care. v. Pupils participate in practical sense activities. vi.Pupils answer oral questions from teacher. vii. Pupils show understanding of five senses topics.
cells.MATERIALS:
Assessment sheets Five senses chart Sound objects Smelling items Textured objects Flashcards Mark book Assessment
checklist

weeks.topic: AIR - Description of air -Air is invisible but can be felt - Air occupies space - Air is everywhere

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Introduction to Air: i.The teacher explains that air is all around us but we cannot see it. ii. The teacher demonstrates feeling air by waving hand in front of face. iii.The teacher uses a fan to show moving air. iv.The teacher explains air is invisible but real. Properties of Air: i. The teacher
demonstrates air takes up space using balloon experiment. ii. The teacher blows up a balloon to show air filling space. iii.The teacher shows empty bottle is actually full of air. iv.The teacher explains air is everywhere: in room, outside, in balloons, in tires. Feeling Air: i.The teacher conducts activities where pupils feel air (blowing, fanning). ii. The teacher takes pupils outside to feel wind (moving air). iii.The teacher demonstrates breathing in and out (air going in our bodies). iv. The teacher makes air visible using bubbles or smoke (with supervision).
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Learning: i.Pupils understand air is around us but invisible. ii. Pupils wave hands to feel air movement. iii. Pupils feel air from fan. iv.Pupils understand we can't see air but it's real. Air Properties: i. Pupils observe balloon
being inflated with air. ii.Pupils see air takes up space in balloon. iii.Pupils learn "empty" bottle has air. iv.Pupils understand air is everywhere. Feeling Air: i.Pupils blow on their hands to feel air. ii. Pupils go outside to feel wind. iii. Pupils breathe in and out, feeling air. iv. Pupils observe bubbles showing air movement.
cells.MATERIALS: Balloons Fan Empty plastic bottle Bubble solution and wand Pictures showing air Chart about air Outdoor space for wind observation

weeks.topic: USES OF AIR -Breathing (most important use) - Cooling -Filling balloons and tires - Drying clothes

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Uses of Air: i.The teacher explains the most important use: breathing (we need air to live). ii.The teacher demonstrates breathing in and out. iii.The teacher explains we breathe air all the time, even
when sleeping. iv. The teacher discusses that all living things need air. Other Uses: i.The teacher explains air helps cool us (fanning, air conditioning, wind). ii.The teacher demonstrates using hand fan for cooling. iii. The teacher shows air fills balloons, tires, balls, swimming floats. iv. The teacher explains air helps dry wet clothes on the line. v.The teacher shows pictures of wind blowing clothes dry. Activities: i.The teacher inflates balloons with pupils. ii. The teacher demonstrates fanning motion for cooling. iii. The teacher discusses importance of fresh air.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Learning: i.Pupils understand breathing air keeps us alive. ii. Pupils practice breathing in and out. iii.Pupils understand we need air every
moment. iv. Pupils learn all living things need air. Other Uses: i.Pupils understand air helps cool us down. ii.Pupils fan themselves and feel cooling. iii. Pupils see balloons filled with air. iv. Pupils understand air dries wet clothes. v. Pupils observe pictures of air drying things. Activities: i.Pupils help blow up balloons (with assistance). ii. Pupils practice fanning for cooling. iii. Pupils breathe fresh air outside.
cells.MATERIALS:
Balloons Hand fans Pictures of tires, balls Pictures of clothes drying Air conditioning/fa n for demonstration Chart showing
uses of air

weeks.topic:
AIR TRANSPORTATIO N -Air as means of transportation -Vehicles that move through air
- Examples: airplane, helicopter, kite, hot air balloon - Smell travels through air

cells.TEACHER'S ACTIVITIES:
Air Transportation: i.The teacher explains some vehicles move through the air (not on ground or water). ii.The teacher shows pictures of airplanes,
helicopters, hot air balloons, kites. iii.The teacher explains airplanes carry people and goods through the sky. iv.The teacher shows videos or pictures of air travel. Types of Air Transport: i. The teacher describes airplane: big, has wings, carries many people, flies high. ii. The teacher describes helicopter: has spinning blades on top, can hover. iii.The teacher describes hot air balloon: big balloon with basket, floats in air. iv.The teacher explains kites: toys that fly in the wind. Smell in Air: i.The teacher explains smells travel through air to our noses. ii.The teacher demonstrates with perfume or cooking smell traveling. iii. The teacher discusses how we smell things from far away because smell moves in air.
cells.PUPILS' ACTIVITIES:
Learning: i.Pupils understand some things move through air. ii.Pupils observe
pictures of air vehicles. iii.Pupils learn airplanes fly in the sky. iv.Pupils watch videos of air transport. Types: i.Pupils identify airplanes in pictures. ii.Pupils recognize helicopters. iii. Pupils observe hot air balloons. iv. Pupils understand kites fly with wind. v. Pupils make airplane sounds and movements. Smell: i.Pupils understand smells move through air. ii.Pupils smell things from across the room. iii. Pupils learn about air carrying smells.
cells.MATERIALS:
